content:
RESOLVED:  That
 
(1)           
the submission of Harrow’s Local SEND Reform plan to the
Department for Education in response to the Department for
Education and NHS England commission, be noted;
 
(2)           
the overall strategic direction, governance framework and
implementation approach set out within the SEND Reform Plan
2026–2029, be noted;
 
(3)           
the proposed governance and accountability arrangements for
delivery of the SEND Reform Plan, including oversight through the
Cradle to Career Strategic Board and the SEND and AP Partnership
Board be noted;
 
(4)           
the £2.1m SEND Reform Experts at Hand and SEND Transformation
Fund allocations provided by the Department for Education to
support SEND reform and improvement activity, be accepted;
 
(5)           
the Strategic Director of Children’s Services be authorised,
following consultation with the Portfolio Holder for
Children’s Services, to approve and oversee the deployment of
the funding in accordance with local priorities, and Department for
Education reform requirements;
 
(6)           
the Strategic Director of Children’s Services be authorised,
following consultation with the Portfolio Holder for
Children’s Services, to approve the Local Area Partnership
Road Map/Mobilisation plan for the next three years, set out in
section 5, appendix 1 to officer’s report;
 
(7)           
the Strategic Director of Children’s Services be authorised,
following consultation with the Portfolio Holder for
Children’s Services, to make any further amendments required
by the Department for Education or NHS England during the
implementation phase of the programme.
 
Reason for Decision: This Ensured a
clear, coordinated and partnership-led response to national SEND
and Alternative Provision reform; strengthened outcomes for
children and young people with SEND through a coherent programme of
system-wide improvement; provided clarity, assurance and
accountability for partners, families and elected Members regarding
delivery of the reform programme; supported implementation of
Harrow’s submitted SEND Reform Plan and associated
improvement activity; ensured the Department for Education
requirements associated with SEND Reform and supported eligibility
for the High Needs Stability Grant and associated reform funding
arrangements and enabled timely, coordinated and partnership-led
deployment of SEND Reform funding in accordance with national
expectations and local priorities.
topline: The UK council has decided to approve and implement Harrow's Local SEND Reform plan, including governance arrangements and funding allocations.

remedies.

operated for the full 8 years possible);
 
(2)           
the Strategic Director of Culture, Environment and Economy be
authorised, following consultation with the Portfolio Holder for
Cleaner Streets and Public Safety and the Portfolio Holder for
Finance and Highways to appoint providers to the Framework;

pricing; improved flexibility and resilience through a
multi-supplier model; supported delivery across a diverse estate,
including parks, allotments, cemeteries and corporate assets;
embedded social value and carbon reduction requirements, supporting
wider Council priorities and maintained market competition and
value for money through periodic reopening of competition.

content:
Approve the commencement of a
competitive procurement process to commission a new care provider
for the provision of high-quality regulated care and wellbeing
services at Ewart House extra care housing scheme to meet the
assessed care and independence outcomes of adults aged 55 and over
(current and future).
 
Delegate authority to the
Strategic Director of Adult Social Care & Public Health,
following consultation with the Director of Finance (S151 Officer),
Portfolio Holder for Adult Services & Public Health and the
Portfolio Holder for Finance & Highways, to award and enter in
to contract with the successful provider.
 

RESOLVED:   That
 
(1)           
the commencement of a competitive procurement process to commission
a new care provider for the provision of high-quality regulated
care and wellbeing services at ‘Ewart House extra care
housing scheme’ to meet the assessed care and independence
outcomes for adults aged 55 and over, be approved;
 
(2)           
the Strategic Director of Adult Social Care & Public Health be
authorised, following consultation with the Director of Finance
(S151 Officer), Portfolio Holder for Adults & Public Health and
the Portfolio Holder for Finance & Highways, to award and enter
in to contract with the successful provider;
 
(3)           
 the Strategic Director of Adult Social
Care & Public Health be authorised, following consultation with
the Assistant Director of Procurement and Strategic Director of
Legal and Governance to take any other decision associated with
this procurement.
 
Reason for Decision:  The
recommendation to undertake a competitive procurement process was
required to ensure continuity of high-quality care and wellbeing
services at Ewart House and to enable the Council to meet its
statutory duties under the Care Act 2014.  With the current
contract due to end in March 2027, recommissioning provided an
opportunity to secure a provider capable of delivering responsive,
on-site services within the Extra Care Housing scheme, alongside
strengthening service requirements in line with the Council’s
Adult Social Care Strategy 2025–2030.  The focus would
be on further promoting independence and improving outcomes through
strengths-based care, supporting a reduction in reliance on
residential care.  A competitive process would also ensure
value for money, service sustainability, and compliance with
regulatory and contractual requirements.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to commission a new care provider for high-quality regulated care and wellbeing services at Ewart House extra care housing scheme for adults aged 55 and over.

content:
Authority to increase the spend
for the Homes for Ukraine scheme, reflecting ongoing programme
delivery requirements.

RESOLVED:  That
 
(1)           
an increase in the total programme expenditure for the Homes for
Ukraine Programme to an estimated maximum value of £4.7
million to support ongoing delivery be approved;
 
(2)           
 the Council’s Contract Procedure
Rules be waived, to enable the direct award of contracts to
existing service providers for up to 24 months;
 
(3)           
the Strategic Director of Corporate Resources and Innovation be
authorised, following consultation with the Strategic Director of
Finance (Section 151 Officer), and the Portfolio Holder for
Community and Culture, to approve the acceptance and expenditure of
any additional Government funding related to the Homes for Ukraine
Programme, including increases to the overall programme value,
where this would not create any additional financial liability for
the Council;
 
(4)           
the Strategic Director of Corporate Resources and Innovation be
authorised, following consultation with the Portfolio Holder for
Community and Culture, to finalise and award the contracts to the
identified providers and to procure and award future contracts for
the Homes for Ukraine Programme, in line with Contract Procedure
Rules and subject to available funding.
 
Reason for Decision: The Homes for
Ukraine Programme continued to provide critical support to
Ukrainian households in line with ongoing Government funding and
requirements.  Funding was provided by the Ministry of
Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) to support the
delivery of integration and support outcomes for the cohort based
on the number of people supported, and the Council was required to
utilise these funds accordingly.
 
In the previous Cabinet report, the Council
expected to receive approximately £2.1 million in Government
funding and planned expenditure within this indicative funding
envelope based on the expected cohort at that time.  Since
then, the Government had extended the programme, resulting in
continued funding and an ongoing requirement for the Council to
deliver support services for Ukrainian households.  As part of
ongoing programme delivery, updated expenditure projections
indicated the need to revise the overall programme budget to
reflect current funding levels and service requirements.  This
included maintaining delivery of support and integration services,
alongside responding to ongoing needs such as housing, safeguarding
and casework support.
 
Existing contracts with service providers were
due to expire on 30 September 2026.  This report therefore
sought approval to update the programme budget and to approve the
proposed procurement approach, which ensured continuity of service
and alignment with governance requirements.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to increase funding for the Homes for Ukraine scheme to support ongoing programme delivery.

Resilience Fund grant provided by the Department of Work and
Pensions for the purpose of the funding described in the
officer’s report for the period 2026–2029;
 
(2)

Crisis and Resilience Fund as set out in the officer’s report
be approved in principle and;

consultation with the Portfolio Holder for Performance,
Communications and Customer Experience, to approve the final
details of the delivery plan and scheme, and any subsequent Crisis

principles set out in this report and relevant government
guidance.
 
Reason for
Decision:  The
recommendations in this report met the essential criteria for the
grant as set out by the Department of Work and Pensions, which had
a focus to improve outcomes for communities and preventing demand
for statutory services.  The London
Borough of Harrow (‘the Council’) had considered where
best to target the funding and the proposals provided a balance of
support for different cohorts of low-income households in the
borough, mindful that activities would be evaluated and may be
adapted for subsequent years.  The
proposal for the eligible spend covered the four CRF strands:
Crisis Payment, Housing Payment, Resilience Services, and Community
Coordination.

content:
Cabinet to consider the
potential introduction of an Article 4 Direction to remove the
permitted development rights to convert a dwelling house to a small
house in multiple occupation (3-6 persons).
 

RESOLVED: 
That
 

(1)          
the background, policy context, evidence base, and financial and
legal risks relating to the introduction of an Article 4 Direction
removing the permitted development rights to convert dwelling
houses to small Houses in Multiple Occupancy (HMO), as set out in
the officer’s report and Appendix 1, be noted;
 

(2)          
the making of a direction with immediate effect, be approved, under
Article 4(1) of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted
Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) to remove the
permitted development right for the change of use of a building and
any land and ancillary buildings within its curtilage from a use
falling within Class C3 (Dwellinghouse) of the Town and Country
Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (Amended) Order to a use falling
within Class C4 (House in Multiple Occupation) of that Order being
development comprised within class L(b) of Part 3 of Schedule 2 to
the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development)
(England) Order 2015 (as amended) (“GPDO”) within the
area identified in Appendix 2 (namely, the entire borough);
 

(3)          
the required notice to be given for the Article 4 Direction
(whereupon the Article 4 Direction will come into force) would be
made as soon as practical following the meeting of Cabinet and that
the Executive would receive a further report at the end of the
representation period to consider whether, in light of any
representations received, the new direction should be confirmed, be
noted;
 

(4)          
the Chief Planning Officer and the Strategic Director of Legal and
Governance be authorised, following consultation with the Deputy
Leader of the Council and Portfolio Holder for Planning &
Regeneration, to publish Notice of the Article 4 Direction and to
carry out and comply with all required procedures, statutory and
non-statutory, including sending a copy of the direction to the
Secretary of State.
 
Reasons for Decision:  This ensured that the impacts of HMOs were
considered and where appropriate, mitigated, by requiring proposals
for changes of use from class C3 dwellinghouses to class C4 small
HMOs within the designated area to apply to the local planning
authority for planning permission, and allowing these applications
to be determined in accordance with local plan policies and other
material planning considerations.
 
In addition, this ensured that the
requirements of Schedule 3 of the Town and Country Planning
(General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 in respect of
the procedure for Article 4(1) Directions would be met with
immediate effect.
 
[Call-in did not apply to the decision above
because the call-in period was waived by the Chair of Overview and
Scrutiny Committee]
[Note: The reference from the Overview and
Scrutiny Committee was noted]
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the introduction of an Article 4 Direction to remove permitted development rights for converting dwelling houses to small Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO).

content:
Cabinet is recommended to:
Approve action to abandon the
home care services procurement tender.
 
Approve the re-commencement of
a competitive procurement process to secure an open framework for
the supply of long-term home (domiciliary) care services for adults
aged 18 and over, reablement support, and children and young adults
with disabilities (CYAD) for period of up to 8 years.
 
Delegate authority to the
Strategic Director of Adult Social Care & Public Health
following consultation with Portfolio Holders for Adult Services
& Public Health, Children’s Services and the Portfolio
Holder for Finance and Highways to appoint providers to the
framework following a competitive procurement process and to
commence call-off contracts with suppliers during the framework
term.
 
Delegate authority to the
Strategic Director of Adult Social Care & Public Health
following consultation with the Assistant Director of Procurement
and Director of Legal Services to take any other decision
associated with this procurement.

RESOLVED: 
That
 

(1)          
the action to abandon the home care services procurement tender, be
approved;
 

(2)          
the re-commencement of a competitive procurement process to secure
an open framework for the supply of long-term home (domiciliary)
care services for adults aged 18 and over, reablement support, and
Children and Young Adults with Disabilities (CYAD) for a period of
up to 8 years, be approved;
 

(3)          
the Strategic Director of Adult Social Care & Public Health be
authorised, following consultation with Portfolio Holders for Adult
Services & Public Health, Children’s Services and the
Portfolio Holder for Finance and Highways to appoint providers to
the framework following a competitive procurement process and to
commence call-off contracts with suppliers during the framework
term;
 

(4)          
the Strategic Director of Adult Social Care & Public Health be
authorised, following consultation with the Assistant Director of
Procurement and Director of Legal Services to take any other
decision associated with this procurement.
 
Reason for Decision:  A compliance assessment undertaken in accordance
with the tender documentation and the Procurement Act 2023 resulted
in an insufficient number of compliant bids across the home care
framework lots.  Proceeding in these
circumstances would create significant risks to service
sustainability and capacity, value for money, and the
Council’s ability to meet its Care Act 2014 sufficiency
duties.
 
Abandoning the procurement enabled the Council
to consider its requirements, understand the causes of
non-compliance, and recommence the process with a revised approach
which met the Council’s requirements, and increased the
likelihood of securing a viable, sustainable, and effective
framework.
 
[Note:  The exempt
appendix to this report was noted].

performance and ability to continue meeting the needs of Harrow

Resolved to RECOMMEND:  (to Council)
 
That
 

(1)          
the Proposed Submission version of the West London
Waste Plan (‘Regulation 19’) attached at
Appendix 1 of the officer’s
report and the accompanying documents /
evidence base be published and the outlined publication
arrangements be approved;
 

(2)          
the Chief Planning Officer be authorised,
following  consultation with the
Planning and Regeneration Portfolio Holder, to make minor
modifications to the Proposed Submission version of the West London
Waste Plan and accompanying documents / evidence base prior to its
submission to the Secretary of State, including inserting any
outstanding process / background elements and presentational /
typographical / accuracy amendments / finalising evidence base
documents (in conjunction with other participating
authorities);
 

(3)          
the Chief Planning Officer be authorised to consider
any public comments on the Proposed Submission Regulation 19 stage
following consultation with the Planning and Regeneration Portfolio
Holder and the Leader of Council and the Strategic Director of
Legal and Governance and to submit the West London Waste Plan and
accompanying documents under Regulation 22 to the Secretary of
State (including any minor editorial or factual amendments to
these), subject to no significant changes to the overall approach
to the plan and policies arising from the Regulation 19 publication
period. (in conjunction with other participating
authorities);
 

(4)          
the Regulation 19 Proposed Submission version of the
West London Waste Plan be used for development management purposes
and determining planning applications related to waste management
development, with appropriate weight given in accordance with
paragraph 49 of the National Planning Policy Framework.
 
[Call-in did not apply to the
decision above as it was reserved to full Council.]
 
RESOLVED: 
That
 

(5)          
the approach to informing the Planning Policy
Advisory Panel on the consultation process, as outlined within
paragraph 16 of the officer’s report be agreed;
 

(6)          
the officer’s report and appendices be noted.
 
Reason for Recommendation:  The West London Waste Plan
(WLWP) was one of the key documents in the Council’s policy
framework.  The current plan was adopted
in 2015 and was considered in many respects to be
‘out-of-date’ in the context of national and regional
planning policy and therefore needed to be updated.  The
process of preparing a new WLWP included statutory consultation
periods.  Cabinet approved the draft
Regulation 18 version prior to consultation in October 2025 and
Cabinet’s and Council’s agreement was now required to
publish the Regulation 19 version of the WLWP and to provide
authority for the Regulation 22 submission to the Secretary of
State, subject to no significant changes following the Regulation
19 publication period.  The new plan was
prepared in the context of the Government’s December 2026
submission deadline (for plans to progress under the current plan
making system) and delegated authority to authorise minor
amendments and subject to no significant changes to submit the Plan
to the Secretary of State was necessary to allow the process to
progress in a timely manner. 
 
[Note: The reference from the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee was noted]
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the publication of the pre-submission version of the West London Waste Plan, updating a key policy document in the context of national and regional planning policy.

To determine the
future contractual arrangements for the delivery of highways,
street lighting and associated infrastructure works from 1 April
2027, following expiry of the existing 18-month bridging extension
agreed by the Leader in September 2025. 
 

RESOLVED: 
That
 

(1)          
the extension of the Highways Works Contract with JB Riney be
approved beyond 31 March 2027 by exercising the remaining
contractual extension entitlement, in a single decision now, for a
period of up to 2 years from 01 April 2027 to 31 March 2029,
securing the incumbent's offered detailed in Appendix 1 to the
officer’s report (subject to realisation the full 2 years
extension);
 

(2)          
the Strategic Director of Culture, Environment and Economy, be
authorised, following consultation with the Portfolio Holder for
Finance and Highways and the Chief Financial Officer, to:
 
a)   
agree the final terms of the 2-year extension under recommendation
1, including the application of the incumbent's discount offer
(allocated proportionately across the contract years 2026–27,
2027–28 and 2028–29) and any service enhancements and
social value to be incorporated;
 

(3)          
the increase of the total contract value with JB Riney Limited from
£110m to £128m over the full contract term including
extension options, be approved.
 
Reason for
Decision:  The
18-month extension agreed in September 2025 was due to expire on 31
March 2027.  Without a further decision,
the Council would be unable to discharge its statutory duties as
local highway authority under the Highways Act 1980 from 1 April
2027 onwards.  Officers had undertaken
an options appraisal which concluded that a short, time-limited
further extension of the existing contract, run in parallel with a
refreshed competitive procurement, was the option that best secured
service continuity, demonstrated Best Value, and aligned long-term
commissioning with the Council's strategic priorities.  The incumbent had put forward two formal extension
offers.  Approving the recommendations
now provided the Council with a controlled path to a new long-term
contract from 1 April 2029 and unlocked the negotiated commercial
benefit.
 
[Note:  The exempt
appendix to this report was noted].

Reason for Decision:  Current forecasting projected an increase in cost
to the current nightly rented model of between 40.5% and 76%
through the next three financial years. 
The cost of accommodation through nightly paid models continued to
rise, while demand for settled housing support has steadily
increased.  This challenge was further
compounded by the rising cost of private rented accommodation,
which made it increasingly difficult to secure affordable and
sustainable options for households in need.  As a result, more families were remaining in
nightly paid temporary accommodation for longer periods, which
placed additional pressure on both resources and staff
capacity.  Through an increased supply
of homes through the HRA for social rent and affordable rent the
Council’s reliance on temporary accommodation would be
reduced.
 
Recommendations proposed would allow Cabinet
to approve a policy framework for acquisitions and for officers to
acquire properties in accordance with this policy, subject to the
funding being in the approved HRA Capital Programme.  Delegated authority, with appropriate
consultation, enabled the organisation to respond promptly and
effectively when additional opportunities arise and where a robust
business case was demonstrated.  This
would maximise the Council’s ability to capitalise on
emerging opportunities that supported its strategic objectives.

Cleaner Streets & Public Safety to submit the application to
Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs to become a
Responsible Body for the purposes of Biodiversity Net Gain and to
undertake all necessary work to secure and implement any
requirements for the Borough to become a Responsible
Body.
 
Reason for
Decision:  Following consultation
with the relevant Portfolio Holders, Cabinet was requested to
delegate authority to the Chief Planning Officer to make the
application to Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
to become a Responsible Body.
 
A Responsible Body was
authorised under the Environment Act 2021 to enter into and uphold Conservation Covenant
agreements with landowners or developers. These were private,
voluntary but legally binding agreements focused on conserving
natural or heritage features of land for the public
good. 
 
A Responsible Body’s role
extended to securing habitat gains required by Biodiversity Net
Gains projects and ensuring long-term monitoring and enforcement of
ecological outcomes.

purpose:
To approve the Social Housing
Allocation Scheme.
content:
To approve the Social Housing
Allocation Scheme.
 

RESOLVED: 
That
 
(1) 
the amended Social Housing Allocation Scheme as set out in Appendix
1 to the officer’s report, be approved; subject to an
alteration to page 22 of the scheme under the title of
‘Victims of Domestic Abuse, the first part of the paragraph
to read “An applicant who is or has been a victim of domestic
abuse”;

 
(2) 
the temporary suspension of the housing register for a maximum of 4
weeks, be approved. This suspension would only take effect in the
event that the Locata system migration and re-registration of
housing applicants had not been completed by the implementation
date of 1 September 2026;
 
(3) 
the Director for Housing, be authorised, following consultation
with the Portfolio Holder for Housing to:
 
3.1.  agree Local Lettings
Plans

 
3.2.  review and update the
financial limits for accessing social housing annually
 
3.3.  review on a regular basis the
required % of Direct Offers made.
 
Reason for Decision:  
 
To ensure Harrow’s Housing Allocation
Scheme:
(i)            
complied with legislative changes.
(ii)           
streamlined priority bands to better meet demand.
(iii)         
reduced the number of offers from two to one, and
(iv)         
strengthened the refusal procedure
 
The Housing Allocation Scheme was a statutory
requirement of Part VI of the Housing Act 1996 (as amended by the
Homelessness Act 2002 and the Localism Act 2011) and should be kept
under regular review to ensure compliance with the law and
effectiveness in meeting local housing need.
 
The Social Housing Allocation Scheme was last
extensively reviewed and approved by Cabinet on 21 January 2021
(for implementation in April 2021) when the demand and supply of
social housing, and the context in which the Council was operating,
were different to now. It was recognised that our current supply of
social housing was not sufficient to meet the rising levels of
housing needs.
 
There were several drivers behind the review
of the Social Housing Allocation Scheme, including changes to
national policy and legislation, a high percentage of lettings
being for studios, 1-bedroom flats or 2-bedroom flats, with a vast
shortage of larger accommodation and a need to review the current
priority bandings to meet the present housing needs. The Scheme had
to prioritise the needs of many different groups whilst ensuring
the Council made best use of its available housing stock and of the
housing association properties to which it had nomination
rights.
 

Online survey on My Harrow Talk platform.
Meetings with stakeholders.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the amended Social Housing Allocation Scheme in Harrow, prioritizing housing needs and making best use of available housing stock.

(2)

Advisory Panel, be noted;

 

(3)

set out above and shown in Appendix 1 to the officer’s report
for a minimum six-week period;

 

(4)          
the Chief Planning Officer be authorised, following
consultation with the Planning & Regeneration Portfolio Holder
to designate the proposed areas (including any amendments to the
proposed boundaries) following the completion of the consultation
and consideration of the consultation outcomes by the Planning,
Policy Advisory Panel, and to undertake any necessary procedural
matters required to implement this.
 
Reason for
Decision:  Harrow had benefitted from an exceptionally diverse historic
environment.  This included conservation
areas designated under the Planning (Listed Buildings and
Conservation Areas) Act 1990 as ‘areas of special architectural or historic
interest, the character or appearance of which it is desirable to
preserve or enhance’.  The
National Planning Policy Framework [NPPF] cautioned that
‘the concept of conservation not [be]
devalued through the designation of areas that lack special
interest’.  At the same time the
NPPF and Historic England’s national guidance recognised the
importance and necessity of identifying and maintaining up to date
records of the significance of local heritage assets.  There were many local areas in Harrow that might not have met
the strict criteria for conservation area status but did have local
heritage interest.  This was a parallel to the existing local designations of
locally listed buildings and locally listed parks and gardens in
Harrow for those buildings and areas that do not meet the strict
criteria for national heritage designation.  Accordingly, this report considered three areas against the
designation criteria for Local Areas of
Special Character and recommended these for consultation as Local
Areas of Special Character.  The local
consultation undertaken would be in accordance with national best
practice.
 
[Note: The recommendation from
the Planning Policy Advisory Panel was noted].

content:
To seek approval to redirect
works to 68 properties from EQUANS to Sustainable Building Services
(UK) Ltdto undertake the SHDF 2.1 decarbonisation works.
 

RESOLVED: 
That
 

(1)          
the variation of contract with Sustainable Building Services (UK)
Ltd,to undertake the Social Housing Decarbonisation Fund 2.1
decarbonisation works to an additional 68 properties be
approved.
 
Reason for
Decision:  Further to the
Section 1 summary, the management team concluded that the original
delivery partner “Equans” was unable to deliver the
Social Housing Decarbonisation Fund works required to a standard
and cost level expected by the Council, which created unnecessary
risk to available budgets and grant allocations.
 
As part of Social Housing Decarbonisation Fund
programme delivery, the Council had proactively responded to legal
disrepair across the Borough’s most at-risk property build
types.
 
Demonstrating value for money; Sustainable
Building Services (UK) Ltd were able to undertake the decarbonation
works for the properties under the current contract as well as the
additional 68 properties at a cost that was approximately 50% lower
than the originally procured Equan’s contract rate.
 
Demonstrating quality of service, from point
of engagement Sustainable Building Services (UK) Ltd had surpassed
the Key Performance Indicator aligned to these works.  They had implemented a robust resident engagement
procedure which had been evidenced with positive feedback from our
residents.  They continued to evidence
quality of work through our contract management checks and
measures, and they were delivering to the Department for Energy
Security and Net Zero compliance criteria which had contributed to
a change in the Council’s risk rating to Amber from the
previous Red rating. 
 
By implementing this recommendation, Harrow
could ensure delivery in full compliance to the Social Housing
Decarbonisation Fund key performance indicators with ruthless
financial efficiency, to the programme extension provided by
Department for Energy Security and Net Zero to March
2026.

internally and continued to deteriorate.  As such, it was considered to be a health and

illegal access despite ongoing security.
 
To enable the early preparation of the
Poet’s Corner site for development under the HSDP, which

Delegate authority to the

content:
Approve the commencement of a
competitive procurement process to secure an open framework for the
supply of home (domiciliary) care services for adults aged 18 and
over, including reablement support, and Children and Young Adults
with Disabilities (CYAD) for period of up to 8 years.
 
Delegate authority to the
Strategic Director of Adult Social Care & Public Health,
following consultation with the Director of Finance (S151 Officer),
Portfolio Holder for Adult Services & Public Health, Portfolio
Holder for Children’s Services and the Portfolio Holder for
Finance & Highways, to appoint providers to the framework,
following the competitive procurement process.

RESOLVED: 
That
 
(1)          
the commencement of a competitive procurement exercise to establish
an open framework agreement for the delivery of home (domiciliary)
care services for a maximum term of eight years, be approved,noting
the framework would encompass long-term care provision for adults
aged 18 and over, adult reablement support, and home care services
for Children and Young Adults with Disabilities (CYAD);
 
(2)          
the Strategic Director of Adult Social Care & Public Health be
authorised, following consultation with Portfolio Holders for Adult
Services & Public Health, Children’s Services and for
Finance and Highways to appoint providers to the framework
following a competitive procurement process and to commence
call-off contracts with suppliers during the framework term;
 
(3)          
the Strategic Director of Adult Social Care & Public Health,
following consultation with the Assistant Director of Procurement
and Strategic Director of Legal and Governance Services to take any
other decision associated with this procurement.
 
Reason for Decision: 
Commissioning a new home care framework would enable the Council to
secure a sustainable supply of good-quality services through a
structured, locality-based model and clear contractual arrangements
to transition away from the current spot-purchasing approach. The
framework aimed to support market stability by concentrating care
delivery within defined areas, enabling providers to operate more
efficiently and reliably.  It would also enable the Council to
improve care outcomes by embedding strengths-based care practice,
setting clear service requirements across specific customer-groups,
and enhance quality and performance oversight.

Engagement with a wide range of stakeholders
has informed the service approach and supply arrangements. This
includes:
 
•People and their families that access
services through the Adult Social Care Strategy engagement
activity. 
 
•Internal operational practitioners and
staff through workshops, team meetings and one-to-one
discussions.
 
•Existing and prospective service
providers through engagement events, group discussion and
surveys.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve a competitive procurement process for home care services for adults and children, potentially impacting various stakeholders.

content:
Cabinet is asked to approve the
proposed procurement strategy for commissioning local integrated
sexual and reproductive health services, as well as HIV community
support services. This will be a tri-borough procurement involving
Brent and Ealing Councils, as the main service is commissioned
collaboratively across the three local authorities through an inter
authority agreement.
 
Delegate authority to the
Director of Public Health in consultation with the Portfolio Holder
for Adults Services and Public Health and Portfolio Holder for
Finance and Highways to award the contract for integrated sexual
and reproductive health services subject to the Health Care
Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 (PSR) being
confirmed as meeting legal and procurement conditions.
 
Delegated authority to the
Director of Public Health to sign the MoU for continued
participation in the pan London Online Sexual and reproductive
health service – Sexual health London (SHL.UK)

RESOLVED: 
That
 

(1)           
the proposed procurement approach for commissioning local
integrated sexual and reproductive health services, as well as HIV
community support services, be approved, noting that this would be
a tri-borough procurement involving Brent and Ealing Councils, as
the main service was commissioned collaboratively across the three
local authorities through an inter authority agreement
and  that the procurement approach was
set out in Appendix 1 to the officer’s report;
 

(2)           
the Director of Public Health be authorised, following consultation
with the Portfolio Holders for Adult Services and Public Health and
for Finance and Highways, to award the contract for integrated
sexual and reproductive health services, subject to the Health Care
Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 (PSR) being
complied with;
 

(3)           
the Director of Public Health be authorised to sign the Memorandum
of Understanding for continued participation in the pan London
Online Sexual and reproductive health service – Sexual health
London (SHL.UK)
 
Reason for Decision:  The Health Care Services (Provider Selection
Regime) Regulations 2023 (PSR), effective from 1 January 2024,
applied to the arrangement of relevant health care and public
health services commissioned by the Council, including sexual and
reproductive health services.
 
Under PSR 2023, approval was sought to
undertake due diligence and pursue a direct award of contracts to
London Northwest NHS Trust (LNWH) and Living Well.  Contracts would only be awarded once the Council
and its partners were satisfied that LNWH met the key criteria of
the PSR, demonstrating its ability to deliver the Council’s
requirements.  Final confirmation would
follow after completion of all necessary
steps under the PSR.  This approach
would enable the Council to meet its statutory duty to ensure the
provision of sexual and reproductive health services for all
individuals in the area, regardless of residency.  The expected outcome was continuity of service for
patients and residents, with no disruption.
 
London Boroughs of Harrow, Brent, and Ealing
had jointly commissioned LNWH since 2017 and wished to continue
this collaborative arrangement.
 
In addition, Harrow had used SHL.UK since
2017/18 to support remote STI testing and
contraception.  The service was
cost-effective, reduced clinic demand, and improved access for
lower-risk groups.  A new contract would
be required from August 2026 to ensure continuity.

Cllr Jean Lammiman – Public health
portfolio holder, Senior Leadership Team (SLT); Cllr David Ashton
– Portfolio holder for Finance and Highways and the Corporate
Leadership Team (CLT)
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve a proposed procurement strategy for commissioning local integrated sexual and reproductive health services, as well as HIV community support services.

content:
To seek approval to enter
contractual arrangements under the London Councils’ Strategic
Partnership for the delivery of the Social Housing Decarbonisation
Fund (SHDF) / Warmer Homes (WH: SHF) Wave 3.

The Leader of the Council received a report
that sought approval to enter contractual arrangements under the
London Councils’ Strategic Partnership for the delivery of
the Social Housing Decarbonisation Fund (SHDF) / Warmer Homes (WH:
SHF) Wave 3.
 
RESOLVED:  That
 

(1)           
the offer to enter into a partnership agreement with London
Councils, which included the acceptance of a £1,990,914.00
Warm Homes Social Housing Fund Wave 3 grant programme, that would
enable completion of energy-efficiency retrofit works to
approximately 144 homes within the Council’s housing stock be
approved;
 

(2)           
the direct appointment of Sustainable Building Services (UK) Ltd to
deliver the Warm Homes Social Housing Fund Wave 3 programme be
approved.
 
Reason for Decision:  This ensured
Harrow continued to proactively deliver warmer, healthier, and more
energy-efficient homes for our residents, and addressed issues of
damp and mould, in addition, residents’ heating costs would
be reduced and contributed to the Council’s Climate Emergency
and Net Zero 2030 commitments.
 
Approval of this recommendation enabled Harrow
to secure and maintain the £2m grant funding allocation
within the London Councils Strategic Partnership administered by
DESNZ, this ensured continued participation in this nationally
significant programme.
 
The proposal also demonstrated clear value for
money, with Sustainable Building Services Ltd delivering
decarbonisation works under Wave 2.1 at a lower cost than the
formally procured SHDF contractor (EQUANS), this would also achieve
full compliance with programme standards.
 
By implementing this recommendation, Harrow
Council could ensure timely delivery, full KPI compliance, and
financially efficient use of public funds, a proven track record in
delivering a robust pipeline of decarbonisation and
energy-efficiency works aligned with both local and mayoral
performance targets would be continued.
 
Alternative Options Considered and
Rejected:  As set out in the report.
 
Conflict of Interest relating to the matter
declared by the Leader/ Dispensation Granted:  None.

RESOLVED: 
That
 
(1) 
the consultation
findings from residents, carers, staff and partners, be
noted;
 
(2) 
the Adult Social Care
Strategy 2025-2030 be approved.
 
Reason for
Decision:  The recommendations were
necessary to respond to rising demand from an ageing population and
increasing long-term conditions, whilst ensuring services remained
sustainable.  They reflected resident and staff feedback
calling for clearer communication, simpler pathways, and stronger
partnership working.  Embedding prevention and early
intervention would help reduce inequalities, improve outcomes, and
align Harrow with national and regional priorities for integrated,
community-based care.

Consultation had been conducted with current
service users, service providers, and internal operational staff
involved in service delivery.

content:
Cabinet is requested to
delegate authority to the Strategic Director for Housing and
Regeneration, following consultation with the Strategic Director
for Finance (S151 Officer), the Strategic Director for Legal and
Governance, and the Portfolio Holder for Housing to enter into
negotiations and agreements that facilitate the provision of
Housing for use as either temporary or permanent
accommodation.
 

RESOLVED:  That
 

(1) 
a bid had been submitted for a purchase in accordance with the
range set out in confidential Appendix 1 to the officer’s
report, be noted;
 

(2) 
the Strategic Director for Housing and Regeneration be authorised,
following consultation with the Leader of the Council, Portfolio
Holder for Housing, Portfolio Holder for Finance and Highways,
Strategic Director for Finance and the Strategic Director for Legal
and Governance, to approve all necessary steps to conclude the
acquisition, in line with the terms and conditions of the bid and
business case enclosed within the confidential Appendix 1, subject
to the acceptance of the bid and all other conditions;
 

(3) 
a budget virement within the HRA capital programme as set out in
the confidential appendix 1 to the officer’s report be
approved;
 

(4) 
subject to a successful bid, a report would be presented to full
Council, updating the HRA’s 5-year capital programme to
reflect the acquisition and acceptance of GLA grant, be noted.
 
Reason for Decision:  Current forecasting projected an increase in
cost to the current nightly rented model of between 40.5% and 76%
through the next three financial years.  The cost of accommodation through nightly paid
models continued to rise, while demand for settled housing support
had steadily increased.  This challenge
was further compounded by the rising cost of private rented
accommodation, making it increasingly difficult to secure
affordable and sustainable options for households in need.
 As a result, more families are
remaining in nightly paid temporary accommodation for longer
periods, placing additional pressure on both resources and staff
capacity.  Through increasing the supply
of homes through the HRA for social rent will reduce the
Council’s reliance on temporary accommodation.
 
[Note:  The exempt
appendix to this report was noted].
topline: The Cabinet has decided to delegate authority for negotiations to facilitate the provision of housing for temporary or permanent accommodation.

content:
For Cabinet to approve the
draft West London Waste Plan for the first round of consultation
(Regulation 18)

RESOLVED: 
That
 
(1) 
the officer’s report and the Appendices to the
officer’s report be noted;
 
(2) 
a consultation on the draft updated West London Waste Plan
(‘Regulation 18’ consultation) as set out in appendix 1
and 1A to the officer’s report and the consultation
arrangements outlined in section 8 of the officer’s report be
implemented;
 
(3) 
the Chief Planning Officer be authorised, following consultation
with the Planning and Regeneration Portfolio Holder to make
modifications to the draft document and to undertake the
consultation (in conjunction with other participating
boroughs).
 
(4) 
the approach to informing the Planning Policy Advisory Panel on the
consultation process, be agreed.
 
(5) 
the outcomes of the consultation would be reported back to Cabinet
in Spring 2026 (when it was intended approval would be sought for
‘Regulation 19’ consultation on the updated West London
Waste Plan).
 
Reason for Decision:  The West
London Waste Plan (WLWP) was one of the key documents in the
Council’s policy framework.  The current plan was
adopted in 2015 and was considered in many respects to be
‘out-of-date’ in the context of national and regional
planning policy and therefore needed to be updated.  The
process of preparing a new WLWP included statutory consultation
periods.  Cabinet’s agreement was required from each of
the participating authorities to undertake consultation.  The
new plan was being prepared in the context of the
Government’s December 2026 submission deadline (for plans to
progress under the current plan making system) and delegated
authority to recommend minor amendments to the Plan prior to
consultation was necessary to allow the process to continue in a
timely manner.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the draft West London Waste Plan for the first round of consultation.

The Leader of the Council received a report
that sought approval to enter into negotiations for the acquisition
of homes in Harrow, to be used for social housing. This acquisition
would significantly reduce the use of Temporary Accommodation by
the Council and mitigate the major rises in cost from the expensive
nightly rented housing market that had been used to fulfil Harrow
Council’s responsibilities under the Housing Act 1996.
 
RESOLVED: 
That
 
(1)          
the submission of a bid and purchase be approved in
accordance with the range set out in confidential Appendix 1
to the officer’s report;

 
(2)          
the Strategic Director for Housing and Regeneration be authorised,
following consultation with the Strategic Director for Finance
(S151 Officer), the Strategic Director for Legal and Governance,
the Leader of the Council, Portfolio Holder for Housing and the
Portfolio Holder for Finance and Highways to appoint an agent to
support with due diligence on the bid and any subsequent
acquisition on the basis that the appointment represents best
value, as set out in confidential Appendix 1 to the officer’s
report;
 
(3)          
It be noted that a report would be submitted to Cabinet to note the
terms of the bid and business case in confidential appendix 1 to
the officer’s report and for approval of all necessary steps
required to successfully complete; and
 
(4)          
It be noted that subject to a successful bid, a report would be
submitted to full Council to update the HRA’s 5-year capital
programme to reflect the agreed price and for the approval of any
successful grant application in line with financial
regulations.
 
Reason for decision: These decisions
were sought from the Leader of the Council as current forecasting
had projected an increase in cost to the current nightly rented
model of between 40.5% and 76% through the next three financial
years. The cost of accommodation through nightly paid models
continued to rise, while demand for settled housing support had
steadily increased. This challenge was further compounded by the
rising cost of private rented accommodation, which had made it
increasingly difficult to secure affordable and sustainable options
for households in need. This would result in more families
remaining in nightly paid temporary accommodation for longer
periods, which placed additional pressure on both resources and
staff capacity.  An increased supply of
homes through the HRA for social rent would reduce the
Council’s reliance on temporary accommodation.
 
Alternative Options Considered and
Rejected:  As set out in the
report.
 
Conflict of Interest
relating to the matter declared by the Leader/
Dispensation Granted:  None.
 
[Call-in did not apply to the decision above
as it had been waived by the Chair of the Overview and Scrutiny
Committee for the reasons set out in the public notice]
 
[Note:  The exempt
appendix to this report was noted].
topline: The Portfolio Holder Decision Meeting has decided to approve negotiations for the acquisition of homes in Harrow for social housing.

content:
The Leader of the Council received a
recommendation from the Traffic and Road Safety Advisory Panel
which sought approval to an Experimental Traffic Order (red route)
to restore safe and efficient traffic flow in Rayners Lane Town
Centre.
 
Following the officer presentation, the Leader
highlighted issues around long-stay parking, loading arrangements,
blue badge access and traffic flow.  He
stressed the importance of keeping the scheme under review,
engaging with local traders, and working with Transport for London
(TfL) on junction markings and access around Rayners Lane
station.
 
The Leader requested that the delegated
authority be amended so that he was also consulted before any
modifications were made during the experimental period.
 
The Leader expressed his gratitude to officers
across for their work in relation to this matter.
 
RESOLVED:  That
 
(1)           
the implementation of a red route in parts of Rayners Lane,
Alexandra Avenue and Village Way East be approved;
 
(2)           
the making of an Experimental Traffic Order (ETO) to implement a
red route in Rayners Lane be approved;
 
(3)           
the Strategic Director of Culture, Environment and Economy be
authorised, following consultation with the Portfolio Holder for
Finance and Highways and the Leader of the Council, to agree the
terms of the experimental traffic management order, having
undertaken further pre-order engagement, and to make decisions to
withdraw the order or make modifications to it during the
experimental period;
 
(4)           
it be noted that a decision on whether to make a permanent order
would be submitted to Cabinet for approval; and
 
Reason for Decision:  The introduction of a red route in Rayners Lane
Town Centre would help meet several strategic aims as part of the
Council’s Local Transport Policy and allow for the effective
enforcement of indiscriminate parking which would help to reduce
congestion, support public transport and improve road safety and
air quality.  Use of an experimental
order was recommended as this allowed consultation with the public
whilst the scheme was in operation and allowed residents and
businesses to make informed representations having experienced the
scheme in practice.
 
Alternative Options Considered and
Rejected:  As set out in the
report.
 
Conflict of Interest
relating to the matter declared by the Leader/
Dispensation Granted:  None.
 
[Call-in did not apply to the decision above
as it had been waived by the Chair of the Overview and Scrutiny
Committee for the reasons set out in the public notice].
topline: The Portfolio Holder Decision Meeting has decided to implement a red route in Rayners Lane to improve traffic flow and safety.
